履修条件
This course is primarily designed for international students in the CSPA English-language programme. Nevertheless, all students who are interested in reading Japanese classics in English are warmly welcome to enroll. Students who wish to take the course are expected to attend the first session.
＊本演習は、主にCSPAプログラムの留学生を対象としています。しかし、英語で丸山眞男の『現代政治の思想と行動』を読みたい、また英語で議論してみたいと考えているすべての学生を歓迎します。受講希望者は、初回の授業に必ず参加してください。
授業概要
本授業は、京極純一『日本の政治』（東京大学出版会、1983年）を主テキストとして、日本政治の構造とその思想的基盤を探求する。
This course uses Kyogoku Jun-ichi's "The Political Dynamics of Japan" (trans. by Ike Nobutaka, University of Tokyo Press, 1987)) as its central text to examine the structure and intellectual foundations of Japanese politics.

授業形態
（内容）
京極純一は西洋政治学の概念を単純に移植するのではなく、日本人の生活感覚・意識・行動を座標軸とした独自の概念システムによって日本政治を分析した。本授業では、この方法論を丁寧に読み解きながら、丸山眞男をはじめとする戦後政治学の知的系譜のなかに京極の仕事を位置づけ、批判的に考察する。
Kyogoku Jun-ichi, rather than importing Western political theory wholesale, built an original analytical framework around the everyday sensibilities, consciousness, and behavior of Japanese people. Students will read the text closely, situate Kyogoku within the postwar political science tradition alongside Maruyama Masao, and engage critically with questions of comparative political thought.

全体の教育目標
Through this course, students are expected to:
○Understand Kyogoku's analytical concepts and methodology for studying Japanese politics.
○Identify the structural features of Japanese political life (party politics, bureaucracy, interest articulation, electoral behavior).
○Trace the intellectual lineage of postwar Japanese political science and locate Kyogoku within it.
○Critically assess the relationship between culture-specific political analysis and universal political theory.

授業の進め方
The course will be conducted primarily through student presentations and class discussions. For each session:
⚫︎ The presenting student will provide a summary of the assigned reading, investigate historical and conceptual background, and explain key vocabulary. Students are required to submit, via Moodle, a report of any length that includes their analysis and critical reflections in advance.
⚫︎ Other students are expected to submit a one-page(approximately 300-400 words) reflection on the reading prior to class via Moodle. These reflections should engage critically with the text and help facilitate in-class discussion.
⚫︎ Class time will be devoted to presentations, peer feedback, and guided discussion.
